name: pathfinder-observability-pack
title: PathFinder Observability Pack
description: Observability definitions for PathFinder. Generated SigNoz dashboards are importable today, and the source pack stays neutral so the same monitoring intent can be used across local, staging, production, and Cedar-hosted workflows.

notes: The VEuPathDB monorepo references Cedar as a server or workflow environment.
Keep routing labels and runbook metadata environment-neutral.
Treat generated SigNoz JSON as a render target, not the source of truth.

filterGlossary.name: site_host
filterGlossary.description: The VEuPathDB host serving a dependency request, such as plasmodb.org. Use this when latency or retries might be isolated to one site.

filterGlossary.name: intent
filterGlossary.description: The classified turn intent, such as new_strategy, edit_strategy, or follow_up. Use this to separate behavior by user goal rather than by raw prompt text.

filterGlossary.name: model
filterGlossary.description: The configured model handling the turn or phase. Use this to compare latency, errors, and token usage across model choices.

filterGlossary.name: surface
filterGlossary.description: The user-facing workflow family. Today this distinguishes chat vs plan_action on pipeline metrics, and chat vs workbench-style streams on SSE metrics.

alerts.title: High Turn Latency
alerts.summary: PathFinder p95 turn latency is elevated.
alerts.description: Investigate model/provider slowness, WDK latency, site-search latency, and Redis stream health. Correlate with SSE and dependency dashboards before assuming the model is the only cause.
alerts.runbook: Check Pipeline Overview, Streaming Delivery, and Dependency Reliability dashboards together.

alerts.title: Slow First Assistant Delta
alerts.summary: Users are waiting too long for the first visible assistant output.
alerts.description: Use this to catch degraded user-perceived responsiveness before total turn duration becomes extreme.
alerts.runbook: Compare time-to-first-delta against time-to-first-tool-call and dependency latency.

alerts.title: Pipeline Error Spike
alerts.summary: Pipeline errors are occurring at a critical rate.
alerts.description: A sustained error rate usually means broken orchestration, dependency failures, or state-machine regressions that are directly user-visible.
alerts.runbook: Check Pipeline Error traces, phase failure context, and the Dependency Reliability dashboard.

alerts.title: Recovery Spike
alerts.summary: Recovery paths are activating unusually often.
alerts.description: Not every recovery is user-visible, but a spike often signals prompt drift, contract drift, or dependency instability before outright failures.
alerts.runbook: Inspect recovery kinds by phase and compare against recent deploys or prompt changes.

alerts.title: Approval Wait Elevated
alerts.summary: Users are taking unusually long to approve plans.
alerts.description: This can indicate confusing plans, overloaded plan cards, or an approval UX that is not inspiring confidence.
alerts.runbook: Check plan presentation quality in Langfuse and compare with approval funnel metrics.

alerts.title: SSE Disconnect Spike
alerts.description: High disconnect rates can degrade the user experience even when the backend eventually completes the turn.
alerts.runbook: Check disconnect reasons, active subscription levels, and Redis stream emit latency.

alerts.title: Redis Stream Emit Latency Elevated
alerts.summary: Redis Stream appends are slower than expected.
alerts.description: Backplane slowness can surface as delayed streaming, stuck UIs, and poor transcript pacing.
alerts.runbook: Inspect Redis latency, stream emit attempts, and SSE event send rate.

alerts.title: WDK Latency Elevated
alerts.description: Discovery and execution both depend on WDK responsiveness; sustained latency here will directly affect turn duration and verification time.
alerts.runbook: Check WDK request duration, retries, and site host distribution.

alerts.title: WDK Retry Spike
alerts.description: Retry spikes often precede user-visible failures and indicate upstream instability, network issues, or endpoint-specific trouble.
alerts.runbook: Pivot by endpoint group and site host; inspect WDK failure traces.

alerts.title: Site Search Latency Elevated
alerts.description: Discovery can feel stalled long before WDK itself is unhealthy if site-search slows down.
alerts.runbook: Compare site-search latency and retries with discovery phase duration.
